newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia jailer says took "tip" for tycoon escape.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia jailer says took "tip" for tycoon escape.

text.p: A prison guard on trial for helping businessman Eddy Tansil escape from an Indonesian jail has admitted accepting money for his act but said it was a tip and not a bribe, the Jakarta Post said on Thursday.
The prison guard, refered to only as SM, admitted during the trial that he received 1.1 million rupiah (about $480) from Tansil to take him home.
"But I only took the money as a tip," he said.
Tansil walked out of Cipinang prison in eastern Jakarta in May this year, ostensibly for a medical check-up but has since disappeared.
An ethnic Chinese, Tansil was sentenced in September 1994 to a 17-year prison term for defrauding state-owned Bank Pembangunan Indonesia (Bapindo) of $430 million.
A higher court later increased the sentence to 20 years.
SM is one of five prison guards charged with complicity in Tansil's escape.
